summary.one_liner: Voyager is an LLM-powered embodied agent that plays Minecraft, continuously exploring, learning reusable code skills, and setting its own curriculum using GPT-4.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides the Voyager code for a Minecraft agent that uses GPT-4 via black-box API queries, without fine-tuning model parameters. It has an automatic curriculum to drive exploration, a growing skill library of executable code that is stored and retrieved for later use, and an iterative prompting loop that uses environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification to improve programs. The Python package is installed with pip, and it uses Node.js packages under voyager/env/mineflayer to control the game. Users can run continuous lifelong learning, resume from a checkpoint directory, or load a saved skill library and run decomposed sub-goals for a specific task. The README says the skills are temporally extended, interpretable, and compositional.
use_cases: Research on lifelong learning embodied agents
Running an LLM agent autonomously in Minecraft
Building a reusable library of code skills for game agents
Decomposing a high-level Minecraft goal into sub-goals
Resuming an interrupted agent learning run from checkpoints
Testing LLM-driven code generation with environment feedback
how_to_run: git clone the Voyager repository and run `pip install -e .` (Python >= 3.9)
Install Node.js >= 16.13.0, then in voyager/env/mineflayer run `npm install -g npx` and `npm install`
In voyager/env/mineflayer/mineflayer-collectblock run `npx tsc`, then in voyager/env/mineflayer run `npm install` again
Set up a Minecraft instance and install the Fabric mods described in the README
Provide azure_login settings and an OpenAI API key, then call `voyager.learn()`
To run a learned skill library, pass skill_library_dir to Voyager, call decompose_task, then call inference(sub_goals=...)
notable: Skill library of executable code that stores and retrieves complex behaviors
Automatic curriculum designed to maximize exploration
Iterative prompting that uses environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification
Checkpoint resume and reuse of a learned skill library in new worlds
Black-box GPT-4 queries with no model fine-tuning
caveats: Requires a paid OpenAI API key for GPT-4
Requires a Minecraft installation with specific Fabric mods; tested version is fabric-loader-0.14.18-1.19
Setup is multi-step across Python and Node.js, and the game world must be opened to LAN manually when using Azure login
The README states the project is for research purposes and is not an official NVIDIA product
Task decomposition can sometimes produce illogical sub-goals that need to be rerun
